docs.forgiving.component: `Forgiving` specifies how far a touch or click may miss this node and still grab it.
Controls are aimed at with fingertips but drawn for human eyes. A drag handle or thin tab is
deliberately narrow — drawn as a thick slab, it would look clumsy — while a fingertip covers
dozens of glass pixels, obscuring the target on the way down. The honest solution is not to draw
it artificially huge, but to forgive near misses.
import { node, Bounded, Forgiving, Draggable, rect } from "game-kit";
Hit testing first checks every node exactly as drawn. Only if nothing would otherwise be hit
does the second pass offer the touch to forgiving nodes. A finger landing squarely on an adjacent
card always gets that card, no matter how forgiving the nearby tab is.
docs.forgiving.miss: A narrow handle on the desk. With `miss: 0`, touching even slightly outside the drawn box hits
nothing. Increase `miss`, and touches in the margin around the handle still grab and drag it,
while direct touches on the neighbouring card remain unaffected.
